auth._gsc_client_secrets_comment: Where the OAuth client secret file is. EMPTY is the right value in a committed file: _authenticate then finds `gsc_auth.json` or any `client_secret_*.json` in the repo root by itself. This held an absolute path on one developer's machine, which (a) published that developer's username and the OAuth client ID in a file that is committed and pushed, and (b) broke GSC auth everywhere else — a configured-but-missing path is truthy, so the discovery fallback was skipped and auth failed with "GSC Client Secrets file not found." even with a usable secret in the root. Set it only to point at a file OUTSIDE the repo, and prefer a path relative to the repo root. The secret file itself is gitignored; this key never holds a secret VALUE.

dataforseo_snapshot._comment: Review chunk X: the market the DataForSEO SERP calls request, promoted out of api_clients.py literals so the GSC pull note can CHECK that the two sides describe the same population instead of asserting it. `country` is the GSC alpha-3 form of `location_code`; change the two together.

gsc_settings._comment: C-C-14: `date_range_days` is read by gsc_performance.fetch_performance_data since 2026-11-15 (it was hard-coded at 90), and `country` is the GSC country filter added by C-M-11 so the client's positions come from the same market as the DataForSEO snapshot (location_code 2124 = Canada). `position_target_max` is read by get_striking_distance_keywords. `device` is the chunk X device filter: the DataForSEO snapshot requests `device: desktop`, so a GSC CTR averaged over desktop and mobile is not comparable with it; 'all' turns the filter off deliberately.

technical._vacuum_min_medical_comment: C-M-02 / owner decision 2 (2026-11-14): the MINIMUM medical score a page must reach before it can be a Traffic Magnet, a Systemic Vacuum or a gpt-4o reframe target. Deliberately NOT penalty_thresholds.tier_1_max, which means 'the highest Tier-1 count still counted as Tier 1' — reading it as a minimum inverts its sense. Re-set 2026-11-15 by review chunk C4 because decision 3 shrank the Tier-1 vocabulary (20 entries -> 13 lemmas, dropping therapy/patient/patients/condition/trauma) and C-M-19 changed the counting mechanics, so the old number no longer meant what it did. Measured on the real corpora in this repo: on the client's own three drafts the total Tier-1 hits went 38 -> 20 on the vocabulary change alone and 38 -> 23 with the new mechanics (39% fewer); across the 56 audited competitor pages printed in the shipped briefings, the old floor of 10 admitted 15 of 56 rows (26.8%), and 6 is the value that admits the same 15 under the 0.39 shrink. EDITORIAL and UNCALIBRATED (decision 7): those counts show the number admits roughly what it used to, they are NOT a calibration — no outcome data was used, and the competitor page text is not in this repo, so the after-side for those 56 rows is scaled, not recomputed.
technical._magnet_max_position_comment: INOPERATIVE as of 2026-11-16, and not because of anything in this repo: it is compared against the handoff's `rank`, and serp-discover stores SerpAPI's per-page `position` verbatim without a pagination offset (review finding H1 / D-C-01). In its 3-page mode the ranks run 1..9, 1..10, 1..10, so a result at true position 25 carries a rank of 5 and passes `rank <= 10`. Against the committed reference run's distribution this filter admits 29 of 29 results. Changing this number has NO effect on the magnet, vacuum or reframe lists until serp-discover's chunk D1 lands and `handoff.absolute_rank_versions` lists the version it bumps to. The briefing says so in the Traffic Magnets section.

penalty_thresholds._comment: tier_1_max is the highest Tier-1 COUNT still treated as Tier 1 — the Surface-Level trigger is 'more than this, with no Tier-3 term'. It is kept only as the fallback for a caller that scores a bare string with no known window; the live trigger is tier_1_max_density_per_1000 (C-M-19), because the same absolute count meant different things in a 60-word page and an 800-word one.
penalty_thresholds._tier_1_max_density_per_1000_basis: The old trigger was a count above 10 over a window of up to 500 words, i.e. a density above ~20 per 1000 words under the OLD vocabulary. Under the new vocabulary and mechanics (0.39 fewer Tier-1 hits, measured on the client's own drafts) the equivalent is ~12 per 1000. Re-set 2026-11-15 by review chunk C4 because decision 3 shrank the Tier-1 vocabulary (20 entries -> 13 lemmas, dropping therapy/patient/patients/condition/trauma) and C-M-19 changed the counting mechanics, so the old number no longer meant what it did. Measured on the real corpora in this repo: on the client's own three drafts the total Tier-1 hits went 38 -> 20 on the vocabulary change alone and 38 -> 23 with the new mechanics (39% fewer); across the 56 audited competitor pages printed in the shipped briefings, the old floor of 10 admitted 15 of 56 rows (26.8%), and 6 is the value that admits the same 15 under the 0.39 shrink. EDITORIAL and UNCALIBRATED (decision 7): those counts show the number admits roughly what it used to, they are NOT a calibration — no outcome data was used, and the competitor page text is not in this repo, so the after-side for those 56 rows is scaled, not recomputed.
penalty_thresholds._tier_1_min_hits_comment: The minimum Tier-1 hit count the Surface-Level density trigger also requires. A density alone would label a 40-word page with one medical word (25 per 1000) as Surface-Level; the same reasoning as risk_signals.cliff_min_sample — a rate computed on a handful of hits is noise.

technical._scoring_window_words_comment: C-M-19: how many words of the page BODY vocabulary scoring reads (the text the density is computed over, and the denominator that travels with every score). 500 preserves the historic window; the change is that the window is now body text once, with <header> and menu/nav elements stripped, instead of the outline text prepended to it — which counted every h1-h3 twice.
technical._position_thresholds_comment: C-C-15: tag_competitor_position's three thresholds, previously Python literals in database.py (traffic > 1000 and medical_score > 15; systems_t2 > 10). volume_scaler_min_medical was 15 and is 9 for the same reason vacuum_min_medical moved: 15 x (1 - 0.39) = 9.2 under the new vocabulary and mechanics. The traffic and Tier-2 thresholds are unaffected by the vocabulary change and keep their original values.

position_thresholds._source: editorial; traffic/t2 2026-03, volume_scaler_min_medical re-set 2026-11-15 for the shrunken Tier-1 vocabulary (see technical._vacuum_min_medical_comment). Uncalibrated.

technical._feasibility_threshold_comment: C-M-18 / C-C-14: the Domain-Authority head-start a systemic counter-page is assumed to be worth — feasible when client DA + this >= competitor DA. Until 2026-11-15 this key had NO reader and the real threshold was a literal `+ 5` in analysis.py; it is now read there.
technical._high_authority_max_pa_comment: C-M-18: a domain whose AVERAGE Moz Page Authority across its sampled URLs exceeds this is skipped entirely as too entrenched (FEATURE_GUIDE 2.2). It was a literal 50 inside main.py's loop, so the one threshold that decides whether a competitor is audited at all could not be changed without editing Python.
technical._max_audit_pages_per_domain_source: operational cost choice, 2026-03 — pages scraped per competitor. It is the reason cluster/EEAT/focus are keyhole views; raising it is review decision 8.
technical._db_lock_timeout_seconds_comment: Y11 — how long a writer waits for another writer's SQLite lock before the write fails with `database is locked`. It was sqlite3's own default of 5, passed by nobody and choosable by nobody, while the Streamlit orchestrator and an audit write this file at the same time. A wait cannot be switched off: a non-positive or non-numeric value is reported and the default used.
technical._db_lock_timeout_seconds_source: editorial, uncalibrated — sqlite3's own default, now named. Raise it if a run reports `database is locked`.

clinical._neutral_clinical_comment: DECIDED 2026-11-15 by the owner (review decision 3, finding C-M-08): Tier 1 is diagnostic and pathology vocabulary ONLY. 'therapy', 'patient', 'patients', 'condition' and 'trauma' were deliberately removed — they are this market's neutral vocabulary, so counting them made the client's own copy score as the medical model and made every 'couples therapy' query Tier 1 (67 of 374 real competitor keywords in competitor_keyword_gap.md are Tier 1 because of 'therapy' alone). Do not add them back without re-reading that decision. 'treatment', 'clinical' and 'healthcare' are arguable on the same test and were explicitly left in by that decision. Entries are LEMMAS: matching lemmatises the page text, so 'symptom' matches 'symptoms' and the plural entries were dropped.

geo_signals._tier_comment: C-M-14 (2026-11-15): the tier is a WEIGHTED total, not a count of present signals. A stock WordPress post (Organization + Person schema from Yoast, a byline of 'admin', a published_time, zero question headings) scored 3 signals and read Strong, while an FAQPage with two genuine question headings read Moderate. The weights live in geo_profiler._SIGNAL_WEIGHTS: FAQPage schema 2.0, question headings 1.5 (+0.5 each for a second and third), credentialed author 1.0, Article/LocalBusiness schema 0.5, Organization/Person 0.25, a named non-generic byline 0.25, freshness 0.25. The thresholds below are read against that total, so 3.0 now means 'FAQ schema plus question headings', not 'any three stamps'.

cluster_thresholds._source: editorial, uncalibrated, 2026-05 — hub_in_degree_threshold 2 and min_pages_for_signal 3 are bounded by technical.max_audit_pages_per_domain (3): with three pages the only possible hub is one both others link to (C-M-13).

serp_overlap._action_queue_row_cap_comment: How many rows each action queue prints in the markdown. Display-only, like reporting.markdown_row_cap: every Excel sheet carries the full frame. The sentence that says `(top N of M)` interpolates this number, so the prose cannot claim one cap while the slice takes another (chunk Y17).
serp_overlap._action_queue_row_cap_source: editorial, uncalibrated, 2026-11-18 — 15 is what the briefing printed before the number had a key.
serp_overlap._source: editorial, uncalibrated, 2026-05 — top_n is the 'in the battle' depth for both sides of the matrix; commodity_high_overlap is how many tracked rivals sharing a SERP reads as commoditised. A local overlap proxy, not a measured index (C-M-11).

positioning._min_focus_tokens_comment: C-M-10: the smallest tier-token total (Tier-1 hits + Tier-2/3 hits across the domain's audited pages) a focus figure may be computed from; below it the domain is `insufficient_data` rather than placed. With technical.max_audit_pages_per_domain at 3, focus was decided by a handful of generic tokens — {medical 3, systems 0} gave focus 100 and `niche_owner`, and one occurrence of 'relationship' moved a domain across the quadrant boundary. 12 is 20 (the review's suggested floor) scaled by the same 0.39 vocabulary shrink as technical.vacuum_min_medical; see that key's basis note.
positioning._source: editorial, uncalibrated, 2026-05 — authority_threshold / focus_threshold are the 2x2 boundaries, top10_saturation the count at which the ranking component saturates, min_signal_rankings the floor below which a low-authority domain reads `emerging`. The barbell is a strategic framing, not a measured law (briefing_messages.json positioning.framework_caption, moved there in review chunk Y17).

youtube_presence._comment: SC-7-YT Phase 1 — YouTube Presence Check. Per competitor (and the client), the official YouTube Data API answers has-channel + subscribers/last-upload/activity/match-confidence. api_key_env is an ENV POINTER only — the key itself is read from env/.env, NEVER stored here or in code (the client_secret_* gitignore discipline). channel_map is seeded by owner-confirmed Phase-1 hits: {"example.com": ["@examplecounselling"]}.

brand._comment: Practice-name suffixes stripped from a domain stem to derive a bare brand token (e.g. 'jerichocounselling' -> 'jericho'). Shared by C1 AI Share-of-Voice and C3 Branded-Demand; matched case-insensitively. Distinct from branded_demand.generic_brand_prune, which drops a derived brand that is itself a generic word.

branded_demand._ambiguous_brand_ratio_comment: C-M-03: branded demand is measured for the DISPLAY brand ('Lavender Counselling'). When the bare stem's volume ('lavender') is at least this many times the display brand's, the demand cannot be attributed to the practice: the row is labelled estimation_basis=ambiguous_brand, its share and growth are withheld, and it leaves the share denominator. Editorial default, uncalibrated, 2026-11-14.
branded_demand._growth_window_months_source: editorial, uncalibrated, 2026-05 — the window length for period-over-period growth; growth is compared over two equal windows of this many months.

reporting._comment: C-C-07: DISPLAY caps for the markdown briefing only — every Excel sheet carries the full frame, and each capped section prints 'Showing the first N of M'. Before this the LIMITs were in the SQL, so the sheet that is meant to be the full export was truncated identically and said nothing. systems_depth_min_t2 is the Tier-2 term count at which a domain's systemic_depth reads 'Systems (Tier 2 only)' rather than 'Trace'; editorial, uncalibrated 2026-11-15, and a COUNT not a density (densities need the per-page word counts that C-M-19 / chunk C4 adds).

risk_signals._cliff_min_sample_comment: C-C-06 / C-M-07: the smallest number of MEASURED ranked keywords a per-run visibility snapshot must carry before a step-change (cliff) test may be computed on it. Below this the signal is withheld and the briefing says so, rather than reporting one page slipping from rank 10 to 11 as a 33% collapse. Editorial default, uncalibrated, 2026-11-15; 10 is the figure C-M-07 asks for. Whether the signal should exist at all before a data source routinely supplies that many is the owner's open decision 5.
risk_signals._pa_drop_min_comment: C-C-05 / C-M-06: the smallest Moz Page-Authority drop between two consecutive runs reported as a Fragile Magnet. The previous rule was any drop at all, so a 38 -> 37 move produced 'Strike this page now'. Editorial default, uncalibrated, 2026-11-15.
risk_signals._volatility_min_shift_comment: C-M-18: the TRIGGER — the smallest change in a competitor's average position between consecutive runs that raises a Volatility Alert. It was the literal 3 in database.get_volatility_alerts while volatility_high_shift (below) sat in config and only set the severity band, so the visible knob did not control whether an alert fired.
risk_signals._moz_cache_tolerance_hours_comment: Chunk X (D-C-10 downstream): how far a domain's `moz.domains[*].fetched_at` may trail the handoff's `moz.generated_at` and still count as collected during that Tool 1 run. Beyond it, an `anchor_texts.status == "error"` is a cache hit being re-served — Tool 1 caches a competitor's Moz block for up to 30 days and can cache it with the failure in it — so the report says so instead of presenting one old outage as this run's. Does not change `errored`; it splits it.
risk_signals._moz_cache_tolerance_hours_source: editorial, uncalibrated, 2026-11-16 — a Tool 1 run is assembled in one session, so a block collected more than a day before assembly came from the cache.
risk_signals._cliff_drop_pct_source: editorial, uncalibrated, 2026-05 — the share of its recent peak a domain's visibility must lose to read as a cliff. See _cliff_min_sample_comment for why the signal is usually withheld anyway (C-M-07).
risk_signals._cliff_lookback_source: editorial, uncalibrated, 2026-05 — how many run snapshots the 'recent peak' is taken from, so an old collapse scrolls out of the window instead of re-flagging every run.

_infiltrator_comment: Serp-compete/src/infiltrator.py — the standalone fragility list (competitor pages with traffic and no Bowen systemic language). `fragility_min_traffic` was the literal `est_traffic > 500` in that module until 2026-11-16.

infiltrator._fragility_min_traffic_source: editorial, uncalibrated, 2026-04 (moved to config 2026-11-16) — the estimated monthly visits a systems-free page must draw before it is worth reframing. Not derived from any outcome.

_competitor_mining_comment: Serp-compete/src/competitor_mining.py — the standalone keyword-gap miner (competitor_keyword_gap.md). docs/serp_tools_upgrade_spec_v3.md specified this block in 2026-05 and NONE of it was implemented: the module held a literal for every value. The key names here are the spec's. Two deliberate departures, both surfaced rather than resolved quietly: (1) the spec's `keywords_per_domain: 20` against the module's literal `limit: 100` — 100 is kept because it is what has actually been running and each keyword is billed, so changing the depth is the owner's call, not a side effect of wiring the key; (2) the spec's `audit_xlsx_path: audit_results_run_4.xlsx` pinned one run forever, so the module now mines the LATEST audit_results_run_*.xlsx by run number and this key is an optional override, empty by default. The spec's `brand_suffix_removal` is NOT added: `brand.name_suffixes` already serves it through derive_brand_name, and a second copy of that vocabulary would drift. The spec's `enabled` flag is not added either — a flag nothing reads is the C-C-14 defect.

competitor_mining._keywords_per_domain_source: operational, 2026-04 (moved to config 2026-11-16) — ranked keywords requested per competitor; each is billed by DataForSEO. The spec said 20; the code has been doing 100. See the comment above.
competitor_mining._min_search_volume_source: editorial, uncalibrated, 2026-04 (moved to config 2026-11-16) — below this monthly search volume a gap keyword is not worth a brief.
competitor_mining._audit_xlsx_path_comment: Optional override. Empty means 'the latest audit_results_run_*.xlsx by run number', which is what the module now does; the spec's value pinned run 4.

handoff._absolute_rank_versions_comment: Chunk X (rank semantics): the handoff schema_versions whose `targets[].rank` counts organic results across the whole SERP. Under 1.0/1.1 serp-discover stored SerpAPI's per-page `position` verbatim, so in its 3-page mode the ranks ran 1..9, 1..10, 1..10 and three targets each claimed rank 1 (review finding H1 / D-C-01). Its chunk D1 landed 2026-11-16: the page merge renumbers to the absolute position and schema_version moved to 2.0 (2.1 with the moz block), which are listed here and in supported_versions, so the rank-column warning retires itself (main.handoff_rank_is_absolute). An empty list would mean no version produces absolute ranks yet. 1.0/1.1 stay in supported_versions because older handoff files on disk still validate; their ranks are page-relative and the warning still fires for them.
handoff._absolute_rank_versions_source: producer behaviour, not editorial — set from what serp-discover actually emits. 2.0/2.1 added 2026-11-16 when its chunk D1 shipped (handoff_writer.SCHEMA_VERSION_BASE / _WITH_MOZ); verified against serp-discover/docs/handoff_contract.md, 'schema_version 2.0'.
handoff._comment: C-C-14: `supported_versions` is ENFORCED since 2026-11-15 (main._unsupported_handoff_version) — a handoff whose schema_version is not listed is a hard fail, not a silent audit. The values were 2.0/2.1 while every real handoff and handoff_schema.json carry 1.0 or 1.1, so enforcing the old list would have rejected every file; they are corrected here. An empty list means 'accept any version'. `minimum_version` and `legacy_fallback_enabled` still have no reader and are removed: the ordered fallback (handoff -> market_analysis -> manual_targets) is unconditional in get_latest_market_data, and there is no version ordering to compare against.

_removed_2026_11_15: C-C-14 / C-M-18: keys deleted on 2026-11-15 because nothing read them and their presence implied the owner could tune something: technical.moderate_feasibility_max_gap, technical.score_normaliser, technical.penalty_thresholds.pseudo_systems_threshold, step_dag, orchestrator.step_timeout_seconds, orchestrator.log_level. handoff.minimum_version, handoff.legacy_fallback_enabled. `step_dag.*` configured src/step_dag.py, which is imported only by its own test and is not on the run path. Editing any of these changed nothing; the live thresholds they appeared to control are technical.feasibility_threshold, technical.high_authority_max_pa, technical.penalty_thresholds.* and risk_signals.volatility_min_shift, each of which now has a reader and a _source note.
